If we could have supplied our ancestors some three or four generations back with an understanding available today of our ecosystem, the passenger pigeon would not have disappeared, Audubon's bighorn might still be found on the prairies of the Dakotas, and many species of wildlife perilously close to extinction today would still occupy viable roles in the ecosystem.
Implementation of provisions of present authority under the Endangered Species Conservation Act of 1969 and the proposed legislation will result in maintenance and enhancement of our wildlife resource for maximum long-term productivity. The legislation that is the subject of this statement and the on-going program for endangered species are, of course, only part of the authority utilized by the Federal Government to achieve this end. Endangered species are only part of the environmental picture. Special legislation is required to provide for the needs of endangered species which might not respond to measures designed for wildlife populations with more normal densities and distribution.
